linear/setup: A linear classifier scores an image of four pixels, x, with one row of W per class: s is W times x.
linear/ask: Which pixels does class zero's score, s zero, depend on most? Ask its gradient with respect to the pixels: how fast s zero moves as each pixel is nudged.
linear/nudge: s zero is row zero of W dotted with x: each pixel times its weight, added up. Nudge pixel one, and only its term moves: by its weight, minus three, times the nudge.
linear/row: So the gradient, partial s zero, partial x, one partial per pixel, is row zero itself: one, minus three, zero, two. In backprop terms, the add copies and each multiply swaps. The pixel values drop out, and so would a bias.
map/sign: The sign says which way the score moves; the size says how fast. Minus three moves it as fast as plus three would, just downward.
map/abs: So a saliency map takes the absolute value of the gradient, its size with the sign dropped: one, three, zero, two. It is written between two bars, the absolute value of partial s zero, partial x.
map/show: Painted onto the image, pixel one lights up most. It is the map's argmax, the position of its largest entry: class zero is most sensitive to it. Pixel two, with weight zero, does not matter at all.
map/other: Each class has its own map. Class two's row is minus one, zero, four, minus two, so for class two, pixel two lights up instead.
deeper/graph: A deeper model is a bigger graph, but the question is the same. Here the score is three times the max of zero and two x zero minus x one.
deeper/fwd: Run it forward on the image two, one: q is three, the max keeps three, and s is nine.
deeper/back: Then backprop from s, starting at one. The multiply hands back three, and the max routes it on, since q beat zero.
deeper/pixels: The add copies it to both terms, and the multiplies hand pixel zero two times three, six, and pixel one minus three. Saliency: six and three.
deeper/depends: Unlike the linear case, this depends on the image. Make q negative, and the max routes nothing back: every pixel's saliency is zero.
